facts.raw_span: a 1½-week history of headache and blurred vision
MRI of the brain demonstrated a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
an HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL
Serum toxoplasma IgG was elevated
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes) with positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii (286 copies/mL)
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
fever to 39.6 °C
generalized weakness
a 1-day history of productive cough
Chest radiograph showed a new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence
CT scan of the chest confirmed extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates with focal consolidation in the left upper lobe

concepts.why: The patient has elevated serum toxoplasma IgG, positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF, and histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites, which are all indicative of toxoplasmosis.

The patient has a low CD4 count, high HIV viral load, and presents with fever, productive cough, and reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates on chest imaging, which are all consistent with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.

The patient has a low CD4 count, high HIV viral load, and presents with fever, productive cough, and reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates on chest imaging, which are all consistent with cytomegalovirus pneumonia.
The patient has a low CD4 count and presents with headache and blurred vision, which could be indicative of cryptococcal meningitis, although CSF studies were negative for cryptococcal antigen.
The patient has a low CD4 count and presents with a ring-enhancing lesion in the brain, which could be indicative of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.
The patient's high HIV viral load explains the compromised immune system leading to various opportunistic infections.

rationales.F01: Headache and blurred vision are non-specific symptoms that could be related to various conditions, including toxoplasmosis, but are not decisive.
rationales.F02: A ring-enhancing lesion in the brain is highly suggestive of toxoplasmosis, especially in an HIV-positive patient.
rationales.F03: Severe immunosuppression with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL increases the risk for opportunistic infections, including toxoplasmosis, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and cytomegalovirus pneumonia.
rationales.F05: Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG indicates past or current infection with Toxoplasma gondii, supporting the diagnosis of toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F06: Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF confirm the diagnosis of toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F07: The presence of bradyzoites and tachyzoites in brain tissue is diagnostic of toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F11: The chest radiograph and CT scan findings are consistent with an opportunistic infection, such as Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia or cytomegalovirus pneumonia, in an HIV-positive patient.

frontier_selector.rationale: Toxoplasmosis is supported by specific findings such as elevated serum toxoplasma IgG, positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF, and histopathologic examination of brain tissue revealing bradyzoites and tachyzoites, which outweigh the evidence for other conditions.
